title: Percolate
tagline: Percolate: RISC Zero-verified private whitelist gating for swaps on 1inch Aqua/SwapVM.
description:
Percolate replaces that with a RISC Zero zkVM proof: takers prove Merkle-tree membership in the
maker's allowlist **off-chain**, and only a one-time-use nullifier is revealed on-chain. Neither the
taker's identity nor their position in the allowlist is ever exposed. The maker's allowlist root
lives in a small, independently-deployed `PercolateVerifier` contract — decoupled from SwapVM's
order/strategy lifecycle — so it can be updated any time with a single transaction, no re-signing
or re-shipping required.
how_its_made:
Percolate is built across three layers that had to interoperate precisely: a Rust/RISC Zero zkVM core, a Solidity contract layer on Sepolia, and a Tauri desktop app for the Maker UI.

The privacy logic lives in percolate-core (Rust): a Merkle tree over public leaf commitments (hash(secret)), deliberately split into leaf-based functions so that rebuilding a membership proof never requires access to other participants' secrets, only the maker (who generates all secrets) touches the raw-secret variant. This same crate is compiled directly into both the CLI prover (percolate-host, used to generate STARK proofs) and the Tauri app's Rust backend, so the allowlist logic is never reimplemented, just reused across contexts.

On-chain, PercolateVerifier.sol holds a mutable allowlist root and nullifier set, decoupled entirely from 1inch's SwapVM/Aqua order lifecycle, updating an allowlist is a single setRoot() call, not a re-signed order or a re-shipped strategy. We implemented a custom SwapVM opcode, PercolateGate, that stores only the verifier's address in a maker's program bytecode (unlike SwapVM's built-in WhitelistCoequal, which encodes allowed addresses in plaintext) and reads the taker's proof from taker-supplied calldata at swap time, verifying it against the official permissionless RiscZeroVerifierRouter on Sepolia, no custom Groth16 verifier deployment needed. This was validated with a Foundry integration test that forks Sepolia and calls LimitSwapVMRouter.swap() end-to-end.

Known limitation, stated plainly: RISC Zero's Groth16 proof compression (needed for cheap on-chain verification) currently requires a Docker container on x86, a constraint of RISC Zero's own tooling, not our design. STARK proving works natively and completes in seconds; the Taker flow's proof-compression step is implemented in the CLI and integration-tested against a mocked verifier call, but not wired into the desktop app in this build.
